title: Signed-in CLI commands require amplify_outputs.json instead of selecting a signed-in site
description:
Signed-in CLI commands cannot reach a site unless the working directory holds that site's amplify_outputs.json or the operator sets PAPYRUS_GRAPHQL_ENDPOINT by hand. Ryan (2026-11-03): people must not need the Amplify outputs file to run the CLI.

**Seen:** from a checkout of AnthusAI/Machines-on-Machines (5.81.0), and again from /tmp, `papyrus editorial context --backend cloud --format text` exits with "Missing amplify_outputs.json. Run `npm run sandbox` or deploy the Amplify backend first." The file is git-ignored, so a fresh site checkout never has it. The advice in the message is also wrong: this site is deployed, and a sandbox is not what the operator needs.

**Cause:** `graphql_endpoint()` and `load_amplify_outputs()` in `src/papyrus_content/env.py` accept only `PAPYRUS_GRAPHQL_ENDPOINT`, or `amplify_outputs.json` from `PAPYRUS_SITE_ROOT`, the working directory or the Papyrus root. The sign-in registry is not consulted, although `papyrus login` already records each site's `graphql_endpoint` from the public `/.well-known/papyrus-cli.json`, which the deployed site serves.

**Expected:** an editor signed in with `papyrus login` picks a site and runs any newsroom command from any directory, with no outputs file and no AWS login. Sketch: an explicit site choice (`--site` or `PAPYRUS_SITE`), then the site the working directory declares (`infra/site.json`), then the only signed-in site; several signed-in sites and no choice is an error that lists them, never a guess. A token still goes only to the registered site that owns the endpoint.

**Also check:** other readers of `load_amplify_outputs()` on the signed-in lane (the bucket, identity pool and publication kind lookups for `stories save-version --images` and `content publish`). A file that is present keeps working for operators and sandboxes, but must never silently beat an explicit site choice.

**Done means:** Gherkin specs for no file, explicit site, several signed-in sites with no choice, and a failing message that names `papyrus login`. Update `docs/cli-login.md`, `docs/editorial-context.md` and `docs/operator-cli.md`.

Related: papyrus-cli-over-aws-cli direction (Ryan, 2026-11-02). Different from cb27a6, which is about the staging build's root path.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Update 2026-11-03: not fixed yet. The workaround is to set PAPYRUS_GRAPHQL_ENDPOINT from the site's public /.well-known/papyrus-cli.json with PAPYRUS_GRAPHQL_AUTH=user. A signed-in site record already has the endpoint available through that file, so the fix should select it from the signed-in site. See PPY-5180e0 for the same problem with PAPYRUS_TENANT_ID.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Tested 2026-11-03 with CLI 5.83.0: stories show, references list, assignments list and context-pack all work with no amplify_outputs.json, no endpoint and no tenant variable, given papyrus --site <site>. With several sites signed in the CLI asks for --site and names the choices. Looks fixed for these commands; issue is still open on the board.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Mostly fixed in 5.83.0 (#1142, #1149); live-tested from an empty directory with --site. Open: stories save-version --images and content publish still need an outputs file or flags; references list without --corpus-key used threat-intelligence on Machines on Machines.
